overview: The Medford City Council commended a resident for performing life-saving CPR, requested a committee meeting with Park Medford over ticketing complaints, and approved a sign variance for a condo building. The council also heard an update on an upcoming survey regarding a proposed city recreation department and updated its designated council representatives for pending litigation.

items.title: Commendation for Life-Saving Action
items.summary: The council commended resident Chris Curtin for performing CPR on a transit passenger and recognized instructors from Armstrong Ambulance and Hallmark Health.

items.title: Park Medford Ticketing Complaints
items.summary: The council voted to request that representatives from Park Medford attend a Committee of the Whole meeting to address ongoing complaints regarding improper ticketing and permit handling.

items.title: Sign Variance for 65 Valley Street
items.summary: The council approved a sign size variance for Maple Park Condominiums at 65 Valley Street.

items.title: Recreation Department Survey Update
items.summary: Councilor Scarpelli announced an upcoming public survey to gather feedback on establishing a full-time city recreation department, after which the update was placed on file.

items.title: Pothole Reporting Announcement
items.summary: Councilor Knight announced that the highway department is accepting pothole repair requests through SeeClickFix or by phone.

items.title: Condolences and Business Recognition
items.summary: The council passed condolence resolutions for former hockey coach Charlie Driscoll, Navy veteran Ernest Casasa, and election inspector Grace Richmond, and approved a citation honoring Kathy Bianco for 22 years operating Wet Cuts.

items.title: Designation of Council Representatives in Legal Proceeding
items.summary: The council voted to appoint Council President Caraviello, Vice President Marks, and Councilor Lungo-Koehn as council spokespersons for pending litigation involving Love Street.

items.title: Approval of Prior Meeting Records
items.summary: The council filed the meeting records from January 10, 2017 as being in order.
